t: Osei Tutu I united Akan chiefdoms in Ghana's forest zone around 1700, bound together by the sacred Golden Stool.
Rich in gold and kola, Asante resisted British expansion through five wars between 1824 and 1900.
Annexed by Britain in 1902, it never surrendered the Golden Stool, and its king is still recognised in Ghana today.
dyk: No one sits on the Golden Stool: the Asantehene is enstooled beneath it, as it embodies the soul of the whole Asante nation.
ev: Asante coalition defeats Denkyira at Feyiase, gaining access to coastal trade
Asante army annihilates a British-led force at Nsamankow, killing Governor MacCarthy
A British-led coalition aided by Congreve rockets defeats Asante at Katamansu
Treaty of Peace fixes the River Pra as the southern limit of Asante influence
Sir Garnet Wolseley's expedition enters Kumasi and burns the capital
British occupy Kumasi without a fight and depose Asantehene Prempeh I
Yaa Asantewaa leads the War of the Golden Stool against British rule
Asante is formally annexed as a British crown colony
